Finding 02 / coordination

Parallelism has a demand shape

A large queue can reward more workers. A slow arrival stream often cannot.

Research noteEvidence pack / current programmeQualification preserved

“How much work?” is the wrong first question. The useful question is whether units are simultaneously available, independent and able to close locally.

Two demand shapes

With 240 sales accounts available at once, two workers crossed the throughput threshold twice. When the same population arrived gradually, extra workers did not improve p90 response time. Four workers were faster in one arm, but marginal tail quality weakened.

240accounts simultaneously available
≠the same accounts arriving gradually

A second workload

An independent monitoring workload crossed at 40 entities. Two workers delivered about 1.9 times throughput and 0.55 times p90 latency, with lower charged cost per alert. Worst-unit consistency fell by 1.5 points.

What changed

Capacity is now matched to ready independent units, not department name or total task count. Quality at the worst unit remains part of the decision. This is a provisional threshold pattern, not a universal scaling law.
